hook: This file is about a child who was recovered from an illegal laboratory after being heavily altered with machine parts. Content note: it deals with abuse of a child through forced surgery, described in clinical rather than graphic terms, with much of it hidden behind redactions. What stays with readers is less the technology than the calm, bureaucratic voice used to describe her.
whyItMatters:
SCP-191 is a well-known example of the wiki using the report format itself as a source of discomfort. The procedures cover bedding, clothing, bathing and power logs, and the routine tone makes the situation feel heavier than any dramatic scene would.

It also shows the Foundation at its most morally grey. The rescue, the decision not to attempt a full repair, and the cover story are all presented as sensible choices, and the article leaves it to the reader to decide how sensible they really are.
thingsToNotice:
Pay attention to the pronoun. The document calls a human child "it" throughout, and once you notice that, every procedural line reads differently.

The numbered list of alterations relies heavily on expunged entries; the gaps do more work than the details that remain. The psychological analysis at the end is worth a slow read: Dr. Glass explains away each sign of distress, and the final sentence about acquaintances is left without comment.

related.note: Another humanoid subject whose daily care routine says as much as its description.
